text: I am 34 and this is advice I would give my 18 years old self. In part 1 I said that life is hard and you need to take responsibility for it. In part 2 my advice is start becoming independent as early as possible. And I mean that in a very practical sense, especially when it comes to money. At 18 you are most likely still studying. And there is a good chance your parents are helping you, supporting your lifestyle, covering your expenses. And that's fine, that was my situation too. But what is important is that you are already moving in the direction of independence. You don't need to be fully independent immediately, but you should be taking steps towards it. Get a part-time job, it doesn't really matter what it is. Waiter, partner, tutor, anything. The point is not just to earn money. The point is what comes with it. You start learning how to manage your time. Because now you don't just study, you also work. You learn how to deal with people. And most importantly, you understand what it actually means to earn money. And once you start earning, even a little, your mindset changes. You value your time more. You think differently about how you spend. And this is the first step towards real independence. Because your long-term goal should be simple. If tomorrow nobody supports you, you can take care of yourself. And there's also another side to this. Your dating life. When you earn your own money, you naturally become more confident. You can go on more dates. You can plan things, take initiative, and not feel like you are dependent on someone else. And the second part of becoming independent is something that many young men delay for too long. Move out of your parents' house as early as possible. Because when you live at home, a lot of things are taken care of for you. Food is there. Things are clean. Life is comfortable. And comfort is nice, but it slows down your growth. When you move out, everything becomes your responsibility. You need to think about food, about cleaning, about organizing your life, about your routine. And this is where real development happens. It doesn't have to be perfect. You don't need your own apartment right away. A shared flat, a dorm, a small room. That's enough to start. But that step changes you. It forces you to grow. It forces you to become more structured, more disciplined, more independent. And there's also a practical side to it. Your personal life can improve. Because sometimes the whole dating process can fail simply because you have nowhere to bring a girl to. And when you do have your own place, it not only solves that problem, it also gives you extra motivation to be more social, go on more dates, and meet new women. And all of this ties back to one simple idea. As a young man, you should strive to become self-sufficient. Not overnight, but step by step. Because independence gives you something very important. Control over your life. And once you start building that control, everything else becomes easier. There is still more advice to come in part 3. Thanks and bye.
